source_refs.raw_quote: EC, EMC, and sodium flurophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The electrolyte was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in a mixture of EC: EMC = 3:7, and this electrolyte was assigned as baseline electrolyte. NaDFP was added to the baseline electrolyte to prepare. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd and Hard Carbon were purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. The HC active material, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), and conductive carbon black (Super P) with a mass ratio of 95:1.5:2:1.5 were mixed and dispersed in water, and then the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. The areal loading of the anode and cathode was 16 g m $^{-2}$ and 33 g m $^{-2}$ , respectively.

source_refs.raw_quote: This result is consistent with our speculation that the reaction between solvent and salt are restrained by NaDFP. Due to the addition of NaDFP, the initial Coulombic efficiency of the battery is increased from $84.69\%$ to $88.89\%$ , which means that capacity loss of the battery reduced after Formation (a process for stabilizing electrode interfaces). Meanwhile, the NaDFP additive decreases the gas production of pouch cells after Formation, as shown in Fig. 1f. Previous studies had shown that the gas generated during formation was mainly from the decomposition of organic solvents, these kind of decompositions always generate a number of by-products which deposit on the surface of the electrode and are harmful to the cycling stability [14]. Notably, the CV (half-cell Na-HC) area of NaDFP is significantly smaller than the Baseline one, inconsistent with the performance of pouch SIBs after formation (Fig. 1e) and following test. The reason for different performance between Na-HC half coin cell and NFM/HC pouch cell is displayed in Fig S2 and these again prove the importance of using pouch cell for battery performance evaluation. In order to evaluate the electrolyte physical properties changes after inducing NaDFP, the concentration of NaDFP effects on viscosity and conductivity at room temperature was studied firstly. Fig. 2a shows the relationship between conductivity, viscosity and additive concentration at 25 °C.

source_refs.raw_quote: Further evaluating battery performance under extreme conditions, $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ and $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ discharge test were followed. As shown in Fig. 3e-3 h, battery with NaDFP remains 871 mAh, 838 mAh, and 798 mAh at 0.3C, 0.5C and 1C where battery without NaDFP only remains 756 mAh, 712 mAh, 695 mAh at $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ . Even at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ , discharge capacity at 1C of the battery with NaDFP remains 688 mAh, where discharge capacity at 1C of the battery with baseline electrolyte only remains 459 mAh. Different from being successfully applied in LIBs, EC is not suitable with SIBs. Because it is easily oxidized on the cathode during the cycling, especially under high voltage or high temperature, which oxidates the lattice oxygen on the surface of the cathode material to produce active $\left(\mathrm{O}_{2}\right)$ species that attacked the solvent molecules, thus resulting in the loss of lattice oxygen and the consumption of the electrolyte [18]. Continuous lattice oxygen loss can lead to an irreversible phase transformation. High temperature cycling and high voltage cycling were followed to confirm the function of the cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) induced by NaDFP. As shown in the Fig. 4a and 4b, the cycling stability and rate performance at 45 °C were improved. As a recent upstart in the field of energy storage, the energy storage efficiency of SIBs under high temperature conditions is one of the main research focuses.

source_refs.raw_quote:
Materials
The sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ , 99.8% min), diethylene glycol dimethyl ether (G2, 99.8% min) and 2-methyloxolane (MO, 99.8% min) were purchased from DoDo Chem. Common ether electrolyte (CCE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in G2 solvent. Weakly solvated electrolyte (WSE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in MO solvent. Co-intercalated electrolyte (CIE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in G2: MO = 7:3 vol%. All electrolyte preparation processes were carried out in a glovebox filled with Ar (H $_2$ O < 0.1 ppm and O $_2$ < 0.1 ppm). The electrolyte salts and solvents we purchased are of anhydrous grade. After purchase, they are placed in the glove box for direct use.

Hard carbon (HC) materials were purchased from Baisige New Energy Co., Ltd. The HC negative electrode was prepared by mixing the active material, CMC (CMC2200, purchased from Daicel Corporation), SBR (BM-451B, purchased from Zeon Corporation) and conductive carbon black (weight ratio 92:1.5:3.5:3) in deionized water to form a homogeneous slurry. The slurry was spread on a copper foil (thickness 18 $\mu$ m) and dried at 80 °C for 8–12 h. Then, it was perforated into a circular electrode sheet with a diameter of 12 mm and a loading of 2.5–3.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ . Glass fiber (GF/D, Whatman) was used as separator and metallic sodium (purchased from Canrd Technology Co. Ltd.) was used as counter electrode. These components were assembled with HC negative electrode to assemble Na ||HC coin cells. The diameter of the glass fiber is 16 mm and the thickness is 0.68 mm. The diameter of the sodium metal electrode is 15.6 mm and the thickness is 0.4 mm.

The Ah-level pouch batteries were composed of O3-NaNi $_{1/3}$ Fe $_{1/3}$ Mn $_{1/3}$ O $_{2}$ (NFM) positive electrode and HC negative electrode coated on Al foil. The specific details and parameters are shown in Table S7.

source_refs.raw_quote: To evaluate the electrochemical performance of the electrolyte, Na $^{+}$ HC cells were assembled. The structural characteristics of HC are shown in Fig. S13, and for HC, the reversible capacity during the first cycle is critical for less sodium loss. As shown in Fig. 3a, CIE provides a specific capacity of 300.5 mAh g $^{-1}$ and an initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 93.7% during the first cycle at 25°C, while CCE and WSE provide specific capacities of 299.6 and 300.1 mAh g $^{-1}$ and ICE of 87.7% and 91.4%, respectively. The three electrolytes deliver similar reversible capacities, while CIE has the highest ICE. The severe electrolyte decomposition creates a thick SEI and affects ICE $^{30,31}$ , which may explain the lower ICE of CCE. For CIE and WSE, the introduction of anions enables the construction of inorganic-rich SEI, and the appropriate number of anions in CIE consumes less Na $^{+}$ during film formation, thus guaranteeing a high ICE for HC in CIE. The rate performance of HC is shown in Figure S14, where CIE still provides a specific capacity of $195.0 \, mAh g^{-1}$ at $2 \, A g^{-1}$ , while CCE and WSE maintain a specific capacity of 204.6 and $131.4 \, mAh g^{-1}$ , respectively. This phenomenon suggests that the ionic conductivity plays a crucial role in the rate performance at $25^{\circ}C$ . The CIE effectively improves the ionic conductivity while retaining the co-intercalation behavior, so the rate performance is close to that of CCE.

source_refs.raw_quote: To verify the practical applicability of CIE, we assembled a 1.2 Ah (163 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) pouch cell with O3-type NFM positive electrode and HC negative electrode (Fig. 6a). Figure 6b shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at different temperatures. At 25 °C, the pouch cell provides a capacity of 1.18 Ah. As the temperature decreases, we verify the possibility of its operation at low temperatures, at -50 °C, the pouch cell still provides a capacity of 0.79 Ah (107 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ), demonstrating a significantly better low-temperature adaptability than that of conventional electrolytes. Moreover, even at -50 °C, the charge/discharge curve maintains a stable voltage plateau (Fig. 6c). Figure 6d shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at -20 °C with 94.1% capacity retention after 300 cycles. In addition, in order to visually verify the practical application potential, the LED lights are continuously powered at a low temperature of -50 °C. The fully-charged state pouch cells keep the LED lights working for more than 10 hours (Fig. 6e). This demonstration confirms that the CIE has good prospects for practical applications, especially at low temperatures. We further compare our results with some previously reported low-temperature sodium-ion pouch cells (Fig. 6f, Table S6) $^{26,52-58}$ , and our work is comparable to most of the advanced reported works, which fully proves that the CIE developed by us has important application value for SIBs in cold environments.

source_refs.raw_quote: The Na||HC half cells with various electrolytes were assembled in Ar-filled gloveboxes using 2032-type coin cells with Na metal and HC. source_refs.raw_quote: In summary, a commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon is fabricated in this work. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, the electrolyte additive adiponitrile (ADN) is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time, and the effects of the ADN on the performance improvement of the cathode material $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ are investigated for the first time. The results show that ADN can promote the formation of highly conductive and stable SEI film on the cathode material surface, and effectively improve the high-low-temperature performance and cycling stability of $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ as the cathode electrode material of sodium-ion batteries. In particular, the battery with 3% ADN shows the most obvious improvement, its discharge capacity increases by 10.5%, 8%, and 13% at the operating temperature of 45, -10, and -20 °C, respectively. For the cycling stability, the capacity retention rate of the battery without adding ADN drops rapidly to 75% after 40 cycles, while the capacity retention rate of the battery with 3% ADN can still reach 78% after 220 cycles. Adding ADN as electrolyte additive effectively improves the electrochemical performance of sodium ion batteries.

source_refs.raw_quote: $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ , carbon nanotubes (CNTs), polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), and carbon black with the mass ratio of 92.5: 2.0: 3.5: 2.0 were mixed in pyrrolidone to form a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 14 um thick aluminum foil to prepare the cathode electrode. The areal density was measured to be 10.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ , and the compacted density was 2.1 g cm $^{-3}$ . To prepare the anode electrode, hard carbon (Kuraray), carbon black, cellulose sodium (CMC), and styrene butadiene rubber (SBR) with the mass ratio of 94.5: 1.0: 2.0: 2.5 were added in deionized water and stirred into a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 9 um thick copper foil with the areal and compacted densities of 4.31 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 1.4 g cm $^{-3}$ , respectively. source_refs.raw_quote: Sodium tetrakis[3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl]borate (NaTFPB, 99 % purity, sourced from Aladdin Biochemical Technology Co., Ltd.) were acquired as functional additives. Prior to their utilization, these additives underwent a rigorous freeze-drying process under vacuum conditions at $-80^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ for a duration of $24\mathrm{h}$ to remove $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ . The Base electrolyte was prepared by dissolving sodium hexafluorophosphate $(\mathrm{NaPF}_6, 1.0\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{L}^{-1})$ in a mixture of ethylene carbonate (EC) and dimethyl carbonate (DMC) (at a mass ratio of 1:1) containing $5.0\%$ fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC). The Base electrolyte serves as the reference for comparing the effect of the additive on the electrochemical performance of the cells. To formulate electrolytes containing functional additives, NaTFPB was added to the Base electrolyte at various concentrations, as illustrated in Fig. S1. All electrolyte preparations were carried out within an argon-filled glovebox environment, which was rigorously maintained to ensure that both water and oxygen levels were kept below $0.01~\mathrm{ppm}$ , thereby safeguarding the integrity and purity of the electrolytes.

source_refs.raw_quote: The influence of incorporating various concentrations of NaTFPB on the NFM111 cathode was investigated through electrochemical measurements employing NFM111||Na half-cells. The rate capabilities of the half-cells with different electrolytes are depicted in Fig. 2a. Notably, the electrolyte containing 1.0 wt% NaTFPB exhibits superior rate performance, especially at high currents, due to its low interfacial resistance compared to the electrolytes with other concentrations. Even returned to 0.5 C, the discharged capacity of the electrolyte containing 1.0 wt% NaTFPB remains notably higher than that of the other electrolytes, recovering to 133.36 mAh g $^{-1}$ . Moreover, cyclic stability tests of the different electrolytes were conducted at a current density of 1.0 C (Fig. 2b). The results reveal that the 1.0 wt% NaTFPB electrolyte delivers a capacity retention of 70 % after 500 cycles at a current density of 1.0 C, significantly outperforming the Base electrolyte and other additive concentrations. Consequently, the concentration of NaTFPB additives was standardized to 1.0 wt%. Corresponding charge–discharge curves are presented in Fig. 2c-e. During the initial formation at a current density of 0.1 C, the electrolyte with 1.0 wt% NaTFPB delivered an ultra-high discharge specific capacity of 150.39 mAh g $^{-1}$ , compared to the capacity of 134.84 mAh g $^{-1}$ for the Base electrolyte (Fig. 2c).

source_refs.raw_quote: Herein, we design a co-intercalation electrolyte (CIE) toward HC negative electrode, successfully overcoming the trade-off between $Na^{+}$ desolvation and ionic conductivity in electrolyte. Our CIE allows ions to bypass the slow desolvation process at interface and achieve sufficient diffusion in electrolyte and HC simultaneously. The free solvent regulation significantly widens the operating temperature of CIE to $-50^{\circ}C$ while ensuring sufficient solvent co-intercalation for ion storage. Meanwhile, the precisely regulated solvation structure enables appropriate participation of anions in the solvation sheath, resulting in the formation of a thinner, inorganic-rich SEI. This interphase facilitates efficient $Na^{+}$ transport across the SEI. As a result, our CIE greatly improves the low temperature performance of HC negative electrode and is further demonstrated in Ah-level SIBs cell pack. Typically, the Na ||HC cell using CIE has an initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 93.7% at $25^{\circ}C$ , and an ICE of 80.5% even at the low temperature of $-50^{\circ}C$ , achieving a performance improvement compared to the existing electrolytes for HC. The CIE empowers the HC to deliver a capacity retention of 93.5% after 200 cycles at $-50^{\circ}C$ . Further assembled Ah-level HC || $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ (NFM) pouch cell can achieve specific energy of $163 Wh kg^{-1}$ at $25^{\circ}C$ and $107 Wh kg^{-1}$ at $-50^{\circ}C$ .

Abstract: A commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with a capacity of 650 mAh is fabricated using the ternary layered $\mathrm{Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_2}$ and the hard carbon as the cathode and anode materials, respectively. $1.0\mathrm{MNaPF}_6$ in the mixed carbonate solvents is served as the electrolyte. 2.1. Preparation of electrolytes
Sodium tetrakis[3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl]borate (NaTFPB, 99 % purity, sourced from Aladdin Biochemical Technology Co., Ltd.) were acquired as functional additives. Prior to their utilization, these additives underwent a rigorous freeze-drying process under vacuum conditions at $-80^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ for a duration of $24\mathrm{h}$ to remove $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ . The Base electrolyte was prepared by dissolving sodium hexafluorophosphate $(\mathrm{NaPF}_6, 1.0\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{L}^{-1})$ in a mixture of ethylene carbonate (EC) and dimethyl carbonate (DMC) (at a mass ratio of 1:1) containing $5.0\%$ fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC). The Base electrolyte serves as the reference for comparing the effect of the additive on the electrochemical performance of the cells. To formulate electrolytes containing functional additives, NaTFPB was added to the Base electrolyte at various concentrations, as illustrated in Fig. S1. All electrolyte preparations were carried out within an argon-filled glovebox environment, which was rigorously maintained to ensure that both water and oxygen levels were kept below $0.01~\mathrm{ppm}$ , thereby safeguarding the integrity and purity of the electrolytes.

3.5. Enhanced electrochemical performance of HC anode
To elucidate the specific effects of NaTFPB additive on anode performance, a series of electrochemical performance tests were conducted using hard carbon (HC) as the anode material. Fig. 5a illustrates the rate capability of HC in different electrolyte systems. Specifically, at a current density of $30\mathrm{mA}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ , the system employing NaTFPB electrolyte exhibited an exceptional discharge specific capacity of $310\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ , significantly surpassing the $211\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ capacity of the Base electrolyte system. As the current density increased to $500\mathrm{mA}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ , the capacity of the Base electrolyte dropped dramatically to below $30\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ . In contrast, the NaTFPB electrolyte system demonstrated remarkable stability, maintaining a high discharge capacity of $174\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ , far exceeding the performance of the Base electrolyte. More notably, when the current density was reduced back to $30\mathrm{mA}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ , the capacity of the NaTFPB electrolyte system almost fully recovered to $306\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ . Furthermore, we conducted a comprehensive comparison of the cycling performance of HC anodes in different electrolytes at a current density of $30\mathrm{mA}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ (Fig. 5b). The results demonstrated that the NaTFPB electrolyte system exhibited exceptional cycling steadiness, maintaining a discharge specific capacity of $226.75\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ after 100 cycles, which significantly outperformed the capacity of the Base electrolyte (144.04 mAh $\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ ) under the same number of cycles. Additionally, it is noteworthy that the Base electrolyte suffered from excessive consumption of active $\mathrm{Na^{+}}$ during its formation process, resulting in an initial coulombic efficiency (CE) of only $60.40\%$ (Fig. 5c). The introduction of the NaTFPB additive effectively improves the utilization efficiency of active $\mathrm{Na^{+}}$ , thereby significantly enhancing the initial coulombic efficiency of the HC anode to $72.40\%$ (Fig. 5d).

Because it is easily oxidized on the cathode during the cycling, especially under high voltage or high temperature, which oxidates the lattice oxygen on the surface of the cathode material to produce active $\left(\mathrm{O}_{2}\right)$ species that attacked the solvent molecules, thus resulting in the loss of lattice oxygen and the consumption of the electrolyte [18]. High temperature cycling and high voltage cycling were followed to confirm the function of the cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) induced by NaDFP. citations.quote: To verify the practical applicability of CIE, we assembled a 1.2 Ah (163 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) pouch cell with O3-type NFM positive electrode and HC negative electrode (Fig. 6a). Figure 6b shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at different temperatures. At 25 °C, the pouch cell provides a capacity of 1.18 Ah. As the temperature decreases, we verify the possibility of its operation at low temperatures, at -50 °C, the pouch cell still provides a capacity of 0.79 Ah (107 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ), demonstrating a significantly better low-temperature adaptability than that of conventional electrolytes. Moreover, even at -50 °C, the charge/discharge curve maintains a stable voltage plateau (Fig. 6c). Figure 6d shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at -20 °C with 94.1% capacity retention after 300 cycles. In addition, in order to visually verify the practical application potential, the LED lights are continuously powered at a low temperature of -50 °C. The fully-charged state pouch cells keep the LED lights working for more than 10 hours (Fig. 6e). This demonstration confirms that the CIE has good prospects for practical applications, especially at low temperatures. We further compare our results with some previously reported low-temperature sodium-ion pouch cells (Fig. 6f, Table S6) $^{26,52-58}$ , and our work is comparable to most of the advanced reported works, which fully proves that the CIE developed by us has important application value for SIBs in cold environments.

citations.quote: To evaluate the electrochemical performance of the electrolyte, Na $^{+}$ HC cells were assembled. The structural characteristics of HC are shown in Fig. S13, and for HC, the reversible capacity during the first cycle is critical for less sodium loss. As shown in Fig. 3a, CIE provides a specific capacity of 300.5 mAh g $^{-1}$ and an initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 93.7% during the first cycle at 25°C, while CCE and WSE provide specific capacities of 299.6 and 300.1 mAh g $^{-1}$ and ICE of 87.7% and 91.4%, respectively. The three electrolytes deliver similar reversible capacities, while CIE has the highest ICE. The severe electrolyte decomposition creates a thick SEI and affects ICE $^{30,31}$ , which may explain the lower ICE of CCE. For CIE and WSE, the introduction of anions enables the construction of inorganic-rich SEI, and the appropriate number of anions in CIE consumes less Na $^{+}$ during film formation, thus guaranteeing a high ICE for HC in CIE. The rate performance of HC is shown in Figure S14, where CIE still provides a specific capacity of $195.0 \, mAh g^{-1}$ at $2 \, A g^{-1}$ , while CCE and WSE maintain a specific capacity of 204.6 and $131.4 \, mAh g^{-1}$ , respectively. This phenomenon suggests that the ionic conductivity plays a crucial role in the rate performance at $25^{\circ}C$ . The CIE effectively improves the ionic conductivity while retaining the co-intercalation behavior, so the rate performance is close to that of CCE.

citations.quote: Herein, we design a co-intercalation electrolyte (CIE) toward HC negative electrode, successfully overcoming the trade-off between $Na^{+}$ desolvation and ionic conductivity in electrolyte. Our CIE allows ions to bypass the slow desolvation process at interface and achieve sufficient diffusion in electrolyte and HC simultaneously. The free solvent regulation significantly widens the operating temperature of CIE to $-50^{\circ}C$ while ensuring sufficient solvent co-intercalation for ion storage. Meanwhile, the precisely regulated solvation structure enables appropriate participation of anions in the solvation sheath, resulting in the formation of a thinner, inorganic-rich SEI. This interphase facilitates efficient $Na^{+}$ transport across the SEI. As a result, our CIE greatly improves the low temperature performance of HC negative electrode and is further demonstrated in Ah-level SIBs cell pack. Typically, the Na ||HC cell using CIE has an initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 93.7% at $25^{\circ}C$ , and an ICE of 80.5% even at the low temperature of $-50^{\circ}C$ , achieving a performance improvement compared to the existing electrolytes for HC. The CIE empowers the HC to deliver a capacity retention of 93.5% after 200 cycles at $-50^{\circ}C$ . Further assembled Ah-level HC || $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ (NFM) pouch cell can achieve specific energy of $163 Wh kg^{-1}$ at $25^{\circ}C$ and $107 Wh kg^{-1}$ at $-50^{\circ}C$ .

Abstract: A commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with a capacity of 650 mAh is fabricated using the ternary layered $\mathrm{Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_2}$ and the hard carbon as the cathode and anode materials, respectively. $1.0\mathrm{MNaPF}_6$ in the mixed carbonate solvents is served as the electrolyte. citations.quote: In summary, a commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon is fabricated in this work. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, the electrolyte additive adiponitrile (ADN) is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time, and the effects of the ADN on the performance improvement of the cathode material $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ are investigated for the first time. The results show that ADN can promote the formation of highly conductive and stable SEI film on the cathode material surface, and effectively improve the high-low-temperature performance and cycling stability of $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ as the cathode electrode material of sodium-ion batteries. In particular, the battery with 3% ADN shows the most obvious improvement, its discharge capacity increases by 10.5%, 8%, and 13% at the operating temperature of 45, -10, and -20 °C, respectively. For the cycling stability, the capacity retention rate of the battery without adding ADN drops rapidly to 75% after 40 cycles, while the capacity retention rate of the battery with 3% ADN can still reach 78% after 220 cycles. Adding ADN as electrolyte additive effectively improves the electrochemical performance of sodium ion batteries.

Abstract: A commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with a capacity of 650 mAh is fabricated using the ternary layered $\mathrm{Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_2}$ and the hard carbon as the cathode and anode materials, respectively. $1.0\mathrm{MNaPF}_6$ in the mixed carbonate solvents is served as the electrolyte. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, adiponitrile (ADN) has a stronger ability of electron donating than the carbonate solvents and thus is easier to be reduced on the surface of the cathode material to form the solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) film, so ADN is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time.

citations.chunk_id: 0061_Song 等 - 2018 - The effects of the functional electrolyte additive on the cathode material Na076Ni03Fe04Mn03O2 f::sec5::child0
citations.quote: $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ , carbon nanotubes (CNTs), polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), and carbon black with the mass ratio of 92.5: 2.0: 3.5: 2.0 were mixed in pyrrolidone to form a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 14 um thick aluminum foil to prepare the cathode electrode. The areal density was measured to be 10.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ , and the compacted density was 2.1 g cm $^{-3}$ . To prepare the anode electrode, hard carbon (Kuraray), carbon black, cellulose sodium (CMC), and styrene butadiene rubber (SBR) with the mass ratio of 94.5: 1.0: 2.0: 2.5 were added in deionized water and stirred into a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 9 um thick copper foil with the areal and compacted densities of 4.31 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 1.4 g cm $^{-3}$ , respectively. The cathode, anode, and separator (20 μm polypropylene) were assembled into pouch cells with a designed capacity of 650 mAh, and the thickness, width, and length were 10, 68, and 127 mm, respectively. The cells were dried in vacuum (-99 kPa/80 °C) until the water content was less than 150 ppm. At a dewpoint of -40 °C, the electrolytes defined as G1, G2, G3, and G4 (Table 1) were injected into the cells. After packaging in vacuum at room temperature for 48 hours; the pouch cells were placed at the environment with 0.8 MPa and 45 °C and charged at 0.05 C for 180 min, followed by another charge at a constant current of 0.1 C for 360 min.

citations.quote: In summary, a commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon is fabricated in this work. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, the electrolyte additive adiponitrile (ADN) is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time, and the effects of the ADN on the performance improvement of the cathode material $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ are investigated for the first time. The results show that ADN can promote the formation of highly conductive and stable SEI film on the cathode material surface, and effectively improve the high-low-temperature performance and cycling stability of $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ as the cathode electrode material of sodium-ion batteries. In particular, the battery with 3% ADN shows the most obvious improvement, its discharge capacity increases by 10.5%, 8%, and 13% at the operating temperature of 45, -10, and -20 °C, respectively. For the cycling stability, the capacity retention rate of the battery without adding ADN drops rapidly to 75% after 40 cycles, while the capacity retention rate of the battery with 3% ADN can still reach 78% after 220 cycles. Adding ADN as electrolyte additive effectively improves the electrochemical performance of sodium ion batteries.

2.1. Preparation of electrolytes
Sodium tetrakis[3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl]borate (NaTFPB, 99 % purity, sourced from Aladdin Biochemical Technology Co., Ltd.) were acquired as functional additives. Prior to their utilization, these additives underwent a rigorous freeze-drying process under vacuum conditions at $-80^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ for a duration of $24\mathrm{h}$ to remove $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ . The Base electrolyte was prepared by dissolving sodium hexafluorophosphate $(\mathrm{NaPF}_6, 1.0\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{L}^{-1})$ in a mixture of ethylene carbonate (EC) and dimethyl carbonate (DMC) (at a mass ratio of 1:1) containing $5.0\%$ fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC). The Base electrolyte serves as the reference for comparing the effect of the additive on the electrochemical performance of the cells. To formulate electrolytes containing functional additives, NaTFPB was added to the Base electrolyte at various concentrations, as illustrated in Fig. S1. All electrolyte preparations were carried out within an argon-filled glovebox environment, which was rigorously maintained to ensure that both water and oxygen levels were kept below $0.01~\mathrm{ppm}$ , thereby safeguarding the integrity and purity of the electrolytes.

3.5. Enhanced electrochemical performance of HC anode
To elucidate the specific effects of NaTFPB additive on anode performance, a series of electrochemical performance tests were conducted using hard carbon (HC) as the anode material. Fig. 5a illustrates the rate capability of HC in different electrolyte systems. Specifically, at a current density of $30\mathrm{mA}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ , the system employing NaTFPB electrolyte exhibited an exceptional discharge specific capacity of $310\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ , significantly surpassing the $211\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ capacity of the Base electrolyte system. As the current density increased to $500\mathrm{mA}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ , the capacity of the Base electrolyte dropped dramatically to below $30\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ . In contrast, the NaTFPB electrolyte system demonstrated remarkable stability, maintaining a high discharge capacity of $174\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ , far exceeding the performance of the Base electrolyte. More notably, when the current density was reduced back to $30\mathrm{mA}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ , the capacity of the NaTFPB electrolyte system almost fully recovered to $306\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ . Furthermore, we conducted a comprehensive comparison of the cycling performance of HC anodes in different electrolytes at a current density of $30\mathrm{mA}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ (Fig. 5b). The results demonstrated that the NaTFPB electrolyte system exhibited exceptional cycling steadiness, maintaining a discharge specific capacity of $226.75\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ after 100 cycles, which significantly outperformed the capacity of the Base electrolyte (144.04 mAh $\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ ) under the same number of cycles. Additionally, it is noteworthy that the Base electrolyte suffered from excessive consumption of active $\mathrm{Na^{+}}$ during its formation process, resulting in an initial coulombic efficiency (CE) of only $60.40\%$ (Fig. 5c). The introduction of the NaTFPB additive effectively improves the utilization efficiency of active $\mathrm{Na^{+}}$ , thereby significantly enhancing the initial coulombic efficiency of the HC anode to $72.40\%$ (Fig. 5d).

citations.quote:
3.5. Enhanced electrochemical performance of HC anode
To elucidate the specific effects of NaTFPB additive on anode performance, a series of electrochemical performance tests were conducted using hard carbon (HC) as the anode material. Fig. 5a illustrates the rate capability of HC in different electrolyte systems. Specifically, at a current density of $30\mathrm{mA}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ , the system employing NaTFPB electrolyte exhibited an exceptional discharge specific capacity of $310\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ , significantly surpassing the $211\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ capacity of the Base electrolyte system. As the current density increased to $500\mathrm{mA}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ , the capacity of the Base electrolyte dropped dramatically to below $30\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ . In contrast, the NaTFPB electrolyte system demonstrated remarkable stability, maintaining a high discharge capacity of $174\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ , far exceeding the performance of the Base electrolyte. More notably, when the current density was reduced back to $30\mathrm{mA}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ , the capacity of the NaTFPB electrolyte system almost fully recovered to $306\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ . Furthermore, we conducted a comprehensive comparison of the cycling performance of HC anodes in different electrolytes at a current density of $30\mathrm{mA}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ (Fig. 5b). The results demonstrated that the NaTFPB electrolyte system exhibited exceptional cycling steadiness, maintaining a discharge specific capacity of $226.75\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ after 100 cycles, which significantly outperformed the capacity of the Base electrolyte (144.04 mAh $\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ ) under the same number of cycles. Additionally, it is noteworthy that the Base electrolyte suffered from excessive consumption of active $\mathrm{Na^{+}}$ during its formation process, resulting in an initial coulombic efficiency (CE) of only $60.40\%$ (Fig. 5c). The introduction of the NaTFPB additive effectively improves the utilization efficiency of active $\mathrm{Na^{+}}$ , thereby significantly enhancing the initial coulombic efficiency of the HC anode to $72.40\%$ (Fig. 5d).

2.1. Preparation of electrolytes
Sodium tetrakis[3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl]borate (NaTFPB, 99 % purity, sourced from Aladdin Biochemical Technology Co., Ltd.) were acquired as functional additives. Prior to their utilization, these additives underwent a rigorous freeze-drying process under vacuum conditions at $-80^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ for a duration of $24\mathrm{h}$ to remove $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ . The Base electrolyte was prepared by dissolving sodium hexafluorophosphate $(\mathrm{NaPF}_6, 1.0\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{L}^{-1})$ in a mixture of ethylene carbonate (EC) and dimethyl carbonate (DMC) (at a mass ratio of 1:1) containing $5.0\%$ fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC). The Base electrolyte serves as the reference for comparing the effect of the additive on the electrochemical performance of the cells. To formulate electrolytes containing functional additives, NaTFPB was added to the Base electrolyte at various concentrations, as illustrated in Fig. S1. All electrolyte preparations were carried out within an argon-filled glovebox environment, which was rigorously maintained to ensure that both water and oxygen levels were kept below $0.01~\mathrm{ppm}$ , thereby safeguarding the integrity and purity of the electrolytes.

The influence of incorporating various concentrations of NaTFPB on the NFM111 cathode was investigated through electrochemical measurements employing NFM111||Na half-cells. The rate capabilities of the half-cells with different electrolytes are depicted in Fig. 2a. Even returned to 0.5 C, the discharged capacity of the electrolyte containing 1.0 wt% NaTFPB remains notably higher than that of the other electrolytes, recovering to 133.36 mAh g $^{-1}$ . Moreover, cyclic stability tests of the different electrolytes were conducted at a current density of 1.0 C (Fig. 2b). The results reveal that the 1.0 wt% NaTFPB electrolyte delivers a capacity retention of 70 % after 500 cycles at a current density of 1.0 C, significantly outperforming the Base electrolyte and other additive concentrations. evidence_ledger.quote: Herein, we design a co-intercalation electrolyte (CIE) toward HC negative electrode, successfully overcoming the trade-off between $Na^{+}$ desolvation and ionic conductivity in electrolyte. Our CIE allows ions to bypass the slow desolvation process at interface and achieve sufficient diffusion in electrolyte and HC simultaneously. The free solvent regulation significantly widens the operating temperature of CIE to $-50^{\circ}C$ while ensuring sufficient solvent co-intercalation for ion storage. Meanwhile, the precisely regulated solvation structure enables appropriate participation of anions in the solvation sheath, resulting in the formation of a thinner, inorganic-rich SEI. This interphase facilitates efficient $Na^{+}$ transport across the SEI. As a result, our CIE greatly improves the low temperature performance of HC negative electrode and is further demonstrated in Ah-level SIBs cell pack. Typically, the Na ||HC cell using CIE has an initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 93.7% at $25^{\circ}C$ , and an ICE of 80.5% even at the low temperature of $-50^{\circ}C$ , achieving a performance improvement compared to the existing electrolytes for HC. The CIE empowers the HC to deliver a capacity retention of 93.5% after 200 cycles at $-50^{\circ}C$ . Further assembled Ah-level HC || $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ (NFM) pouch cell can achieve specific energy of $163 Wh kg^{-1}$ at $25^{\circ}C$ and $107 Wh kg^{-1}$ at $-50^{\circ}C$ .

evidence_ledger.quote:
3.5. Enhanced electrochemical performance of HC anode
To elucidate the specific effects of NaTFPB additive on anode performance, a series of electrochemical performance tests were conducted using hard carbon (HC) as the anode material. Fig. 5a illustrates the rate capability of HC in different electrolyte systems. Specifically, at a current density of $30\mathrm{mA}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ , the system employing NaTFPB electrolyte exhibited an exceptional discharge specific capacity of $310\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ , significantly surpassing the $211\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ capacity of the Base electrolyte system. As the current density increased to $500\mathrm{mA}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ , the capacity of the Base electrolyte dropped dramatically to below $30\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ . In contrast, the NaTFPB electrolyte system demonstrated remarkable stability, maintaining a high discharge capacity of $174\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ , far exceeding the performance of the Base electrolyte. More notably, when the current density was reduced back to $30\mathrm{mA}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ , the capacity of the NaTFPB electrolyte system almost fully recovered to $306\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ . Furthermore, we conducted a comprehensive comparison of the cycling performance of HC anodes in different electrolytes at a current density of $30\mathrm{mA}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ (Fig. 5b). The results demonstrated that the NaTFPB electrolyte system exhibited exceptional cycling steadiness, maintaining a discharge specific capacity of $226.75\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ after 100 cycles, which significantly outperformed the capacity of the Base electrolyte (144.04 mAh $\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ ) under the same number of cycles. Additionally, it is noteworthy that the Base electrolyte suffered from excessive consumption of active $\mathrm{Na^{+}}$ during its formation process, resulting in an initial coulombic efficiency (CE) of only $60.40\%$ (Fig. 5c). The introduction of the NaTFPB additive effectively improves the utilization efficiency of active $\mathrm{Na^{+}}$ , thereby significantly enhancing the initial coulombic efficiency of the HC anode to $72.40\%$ (Fig. 5d).

citations.quote: To evaluate the electrochemical performance of the electrolyte, Na $^{+}$ HC cells were assembled. The structural characteristics of HC are shown in Fig. S13, and for HC, the reversible capacity during the first cycle is critical for less sodium loss. As shown in Fig. 3a, CIE provides a specific capacity of 300.5 mAh g $^{-1}$ and an initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 93.7% during the first cycle at 25°C, while CCE and WSE provide specific capacities of 299.6 and 300.1 mAh g $^{-1}$ and ICE of 87.7% and 91.4%, respectively. The three electrolytes deliver similar reversible capacities, while CIE has the highest ICE. The severe electrolyte decomposition creates a thick SEI and affects ICE $^{30,31}$ , which may explain the lower ICE of CCE. For CIE and WSE, the introduction of anions enables the construction of inorganic-rich SEI, and the appropriate number of anions in CIE consumes less Na $^{+}$ during film formation, thus guaranteeing a high ICE for HC in CIE. The rate performance of HC is shown in Figure S14, where CIE still provides a specific capacity of $195.0 \, mAh g^{-1}$ at $2 \, A g^{-1}$ , while CCE and WSE maintain a specific capacity of 204.6 and $131.4 \, mAh g^{-1}$ , respectively. This phenomenon suggests that the ionic conductivity plays a crucial role in the rate performance at $25^{\circ}C$ . The CIE effectively improves the ionic conductivity while retaining the co-intercalation behavior, so the rate performance is close to that of CCE.

citations.quote: Herein, we design a co-intercalation electrolyte (CIE) toward HC negative electrode, successfully overcoming the trade-off between $Na^{+}$ desolvation and ionic conductivity in electrolyte. Our CIE allows ions to bypass the slow desolvation process at interface and achieve sufficient diffusion in electrolyte and HC simultaneously. The free solvent regulation significantly widens the operating temperature of CIE to $-50^{\circ}C$ while ensuring sufficient solvent co-intercalation for ion storage. Meanwhile, the precisely regulated solvation structure enables appropriate participation of anions in the solvation sheath, resulting in the formation of a thinner, inorganic-rich SEI. This interphase facilitates efficient $Na^{+}$ transport across the SEI. As a result, our CIE greatly improves the low temperature performance of HC negative electrode and is further demonstrated in Ah-level SIBs cell pack. Typically, the Na ||HC cell using CIE has an initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 93.7% at $25^{\circ}C$ , and an ICE of 80.5% even at the low temperature of $-50^{\circ}C$ , achieving a performance improvement compared to the existing electrolytes for HC. The CIE empowers the HC to deliver a capacity retention of 93.5% after 200 cycles at $-50^{\circ}C$ . Further assembled Ah-level HC || $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ (NFM) pouch cell can achieve specific energy of $163 Wh kg^{-1}$ at $25^{\circ}C$ and $107 Wh kg^{-1}$ at $-50^{\circ}C$ .

Abstract: A commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with a capacity of 650 mAh is fabricated using the ternary layered $\mathrm{Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_2}$ and the hard carbon as the cathode and anode materials, respectively. $1.0\mathrm{MNaPF}_6$ in the mixed carbonate solvents is served as the electrolyte. citations.quote: In summary, a commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon is fabricated in this work. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, the electrolyte additive adiponitrile (ADN) is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time, and the effects of the ADN on the performance improvement of the cathode material $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ are investigated for the first time. The results show that ADN can promote the formation of highly conductive and stable SEI film on the cathode material surface, and effectively improve the high-low-temperature performance and cycling stability of $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ as the cathode electrode material of sodium-ion batteries. In particular, the battery with 3% ADN shows the most obvious improvement, its discharge capacity increases by 10.5%, 8%, and 13% at the operating temperature of 45, -10, and -20 °C, respectively. For the cycling stability, the capacity retention rate of the battery without adding ADN drops rapidly to 75% after 40 cycles, while the capacity retention rate of the battery with 3% ADN can still reach 78% after 220 cycles. Adding ADN as electrolyte additive effectively improves the electrochemical performance of sodium ion batteries.

citations.quote: $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ , carbon nanotubes (CNTs), polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), and carbon black with the mass ratio of 92.5: 2.0: 3.5: 2.0 were mixed in pyrrolidone to form a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 14 um thick aluminum foil to prepare the cathode electrode. The areal density was measured to be 10.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ , and the compacted density was 2.1 g cm $^{-3}$ . To prepare the anode electrode, hard carbon (Kuraray), carbon black, cellulose sodium (CMC), and styrene butadiene rubber (SBR) with the mass ratio of 94.5: 1.0: 2.0: 2.5 were added in deionized water and stirred into a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 9 um thick copper foil with the areal and compacted densities of 4.31 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 1.4 g cm $^{-3}$ , respectively. The cathode, anode, and separator (20 μm polypropylene) were assembled into pouch cells with a designed capacity of 650 mAh, and the thickness, width, and length were 10, 68, and 127 mm, respectively. The cells were dried in vacuum (-99 kPa/80 °C) until the water content was less than 150 ppm. At a dewpoint of -40 °C, the electrolytes defined as G1, G2, G3, and G4 (Table 1) were injected into the cells. After packaging in vacuum at room temperature for 48 hours; the pouch cells were placed at the environment with 0.8 MPa and 45 °C and charged at 0.05 C for 180 min, followed by another charge at a constant current of 0.1 C for 360 min.

association_citations.quote: $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ , carbon nanotubes (CNTs), polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), and carbon black with the mass ratio of 92.5: 2.0: 3.5: 2.0 were mixed in pyrrolidone to form a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 14 um thick aluminum foil to prepare the cathode electrode. The areal density was measured to be 10.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ , and the compacted density was 2.1 g cm $^{-3}$ . To prepare the anode electrode, hard carbon (Kuraray), carbon black, cellulose sodium (CMC), and styrene butadiene rubber (SBR) with the mass ratio of 94.5: 1.0: 2.0: 2.5 were added in deionized water and stirred into a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 9 um thick copper foil with the areal and compacted densities of 4.31 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 1.4 g cm $^{-3}$ , respectively. The cathode, anode, and separator (20 μm polypropylene) were assembled into pouch cells with a designed capacity of 650 mAh, and the thickness, width, and length were 10, 68, and 127 mm, respectively. The cells were dried in vacuum (-99 kPa/80 °C) until the water content was less than 150 ppm. At a dewpoint of -40 °C, the electrolytes defined as G1, G2, G3, and G4 (Table 1) were injected into the cells. After packaging in vacuum at room temperature for 48 hours; the pouch cells were placed at the environment with 0.8 MPa and 45 °C and charged at 0.05 C for 180 min, followed by another charge at a constant current of 0.1 C for 360 min.

Abstract: A commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with a capacity of 650 mAh is fabricated using the ternary layered $\mathrm{Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_2}$ and the hard carbon as the cathode and anode materials, respectively. $1.0\mathrm{MNaPF}_6$ in the mixed carbonate solvents is served as the electrolyte. 2.1. Preparation of electrolytes
Sodium tetrakis[3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl]borate (NaTFPB, 99 % purity, sourced from Aladdin Biochemical Technology Co., Ltd.) were acquired as functional additives. Prior to their utilization, these additives underwent a rigorous freeze-drying process under vacuum conditions at $-80^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ for a duration of $24\mathrm{h}$ to remove $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ . The Base electrolyte was prepared by dissolving sodium hexafluorophosphate $(\mathrm{NaPF}_6, 1.0\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{L}^{-1})$ in a mixture of ethylene carbonate (EC) and dimethyl carbonate (DMC) (at a mass ratio of 1:1) containing $5.0\%$ fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC). The Base electrolyte serves as the reference for comparing the effect of the additive on the electrochemical performance of the cells. To formulate electrolytes containing functional additives, NaTFPB was added to the Base electrolyte at various concentrations, as illustrated in Fig. S1. All electrolyte preparations were carried out within an argon-filled glovebox environment, which was rigorously maintained to ensure that both water and oxygen levels were kept below $0.01~\mathrm{ppm}$ , thereby safeguarding the integrity and purity of the electrolytes.

citations.quote:
3.5. Enhanced electrochemical performance of HC anode
To elucidate the specific effects of NaTFPB additive on anode performance, a series of electrochemical performance tests were conducted using hard carbon (HC) as the anode material. Fig. 5a illustrates the rate capability of HC in different electrolyte systems. Specifically, at a current density of $30\mathrm{mA}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ , the system employing NaTFPB electrolyte exhibited an exceptional discharge specific capacity of $310\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ , significantly surpassing the $211\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ capacity of the Base electrolyte system. As the current density increased to $500\mathrm{mA}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ , the capacity of the Base electrolyte dropped dramatically to below $30\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ . In contrast, the NaTFPB electrolyte system demonstrated remarkable stability, maintaining a high discharge capacity of $174\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ , far exceeding the performance of the Base electrolyte. More notably, when the current density was reduced back to $30\mathrm{mA}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ , the capacity of the NaTFPB electrolyte system almost fully recovered to $306\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ . Furthermore, we conducted a comprehensive comparison of the cycling performance of HC anodes in different electrolytes at a current density of $30\mathrm{mA}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ (Fig. 5b). The results demonstrated that the NaTFPB electrolyte system exhibited exceptional cycling steadiness, maintaining a discharge specific capacity of $226.75\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ after 100 cycles, which significantly outperformed the capacity of the Base electrolyte (144.04 mAh $\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ ) under the same number of cycles. Additionally, it is noteworthy that the Base electrolyte suffered from excessive consumption of active $\mathrm{Na^{+}}$ during its formation process, resulting in an initial coulombic efficiency (CE) of only $60.40\%$ (Fig. 5c). The introduction of the NaTFPB additive effectively improves the utilization efficiency of active $\mathrm{Na^{+}}$ , thereby significantly enhancing the initial coulombic efficiency of the HC anode to $72.40\%$ (Fig. 5d).

Materials
The sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ , 99.8% min), diethylene glycol dimethyl ether (G2, 99.8% min) and 2-methyloxolane (MO, 99.8% min) were purchased from DoDo Chem. Common ether electrolyte (CCE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in G2 solvent. Weakly solvated electrolyte (WSE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in MO solvent. Co-intercalated electrolyte (CIE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in G2: MO = 7:3 vol%. All electrolyte preparation processes were carried out in a glovebox filled with Ar (H $_2$ O < 0.1 ppm and O $_2$ < 0.1 ppm). The electrolyte salts and solvents we purchased are of anhydrous grade. After purchase, they are placed in the glove box for direct use.

Hard carbon (HC) materials were purchased from Baisige New Energy Co., Ltd. The HC negative electrode was prepared by mixing the active material, CMC (CMC2200, purchased from Daicel Corporation), SBR (BM-451B, purchased from Zeon Corporation) and conductive carbon black (weight ratio 92:1.5:3.5:3) in deionized water to form a homogeneous slurry. The slurry was spread on a copper foil (thickness 18 $\mu$ m) and dried at 80 °C for 8–12 h. Then, it was perforated into a circular electrode sheet with a diameter of 12 mm and a loading of 2.5–3.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ . Glass fiber (GF/D, Whatman) was used as separator and metallic sodium (purchased from Canrd Technology Co. Ltd.) was used as counter electrode. These components were assembled with HC negative electrode to assemble Na ||HC coin cells. The diameter of the glass fiber is 16 mm and the thickness is 0.68 mm. The diameter of the sodium metal electrode is 15.6 mm and the thickness is 0.4 mm.

The Ah-level pouch batteries were composed of O3-NaNi $_{1/3}$ Fe $_{1/3}$ Mn $_{1/3}$ O $_{2}$ (NFM) positive electrode and HC negative electrode coated on Al foil. The specific details and parameters are shown in Table S7.

citations.quote: To verify the practical applicability of CIE, we assembled a 1.2 Ah (163 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) pouch cell with O3-type NFM positive electrode and HC negative electrode (Fig. 6a). Figure 6b shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at different temperatures. At 25 °C, the pouch cell provides a capacity of 1.18 Ah. As the temperature decreases, we verify the possibility of its operation at low temperatures, at -50 °C, the pouch cell still provides a capacity of 0.79 Ah (107 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ), demonstrating a significantly better low-temperature adaptability than that of conventional electrolytes. Moreover, even at -50 °C, the charge/discharge curve maintains a stable voltage plateau (Fig. 6c). Figure 6d shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at -20 °C with 94.1% capacity retention after 300 cycles. In addition, in order to visually verify the practical application potential, the LED lights are continuously powered at a low temperature of -50 °C. The fully-charged state pouch cells keep the LED lights working for more than 10 hours (Fig. 6e). This demonstration confirms that the CIE has good prospects for practical applications, especially at low temperatures. We further compare our results with some previously reported low-temperature sodium-ion pouch cells (Fig. 6f, Table S6) $^{26,52-58}$ , and our work is comparable to most of the advanced reported works, which fully proves that the CIE developed by us has important application value for SIBs in cold environments.

The structural characteristics of HC are shown in Fig. S13, and for HC, the reversible capacity during the first cycle is critical for less sodium loss. As shown in Fig. 3a, CIE provides a specific capacity of 300.5 mAh g $^{-1}$ and an initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 93.7% during the first cycle at 25°C, while CCE and WSE provide specific capacities of 299.6 and 300.1 mAh g $^{-1}$ and ICE of 87.7% and 91.4%, respectively. The severe electrolyte decomposition creates a thick SEI and affects ICE $^{30,31}$ , which may explain the lower ICE of CCE. For CIE and WSE, the introduction of anions enables the construction of inorganic-rich SEI, and the appropriate number of anions in CIE consumes less Na $^{+}$ during film formation, thus guaranteeing a high ICE for HC in CIE. The rate performance of HC is shown in Figure S14, where CIE still provides a specific capacity of $195.0 \, mAh g^{-1}$ at $2 \, A g^{-1}$ , while CCE and WSE maintain a specific capacity of 204.6 and $131.4 \, mAh g^{-1}$ , respectively. This phenomenon suggests that the ionic conductivity plays a crucial role in the rate performance at $25^{\circ}C$ . The CIE effectively improves the ionic conductivity while retaining the co-intercalation behavior, so the rate performance is close to that of CCE.

citations.quote: Herein, we design a co-intercalation electrolyte (CIE) toward HC negative electrode, successfully overcoming the trade-off between $Na^{+}$ desolvation and ionic conductivity in electrolyte. Our CIE allows ions to bypass the slow desolvation process at interface and achieve sufficient diffusion in electrolyte and HC simultaneously. The free solvent regulation significantly widens the operating temperature of CIE to $-50^{\circ}C$ while ensuring sufficient solvent co-intercalation for ion storage. Meanwhile, the precisely regulated solvation structure enables appropriate participation of anions in the solvation sheath, resulting in the formation of a thinner, inorganic-rich SEI. This interphase facilitates efficient $Na^{+}$ transport across the SEI. As a result, our CIE greatly improves the low temperature performance of HC negative electrode and is further demonstrated in Ah-level SIBs cell pack. Typically, the Na ||HC cell using CIE has an initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 93.7% at $25^{\circ}C$ , and an ICE of 80.5% even at the low temperature of $-50^{\circ}C$ , achieving a performance improvement compared to the existing electrolytes for HC. The CIE empowers the HC to deliver a capacity retention of 93.5% after 200 cycles at $-50^{\circ}C$ . Further assembled Ah-level HC || $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ (NFM) pouch cell can achieve specific energy of $163 Wh kg^{-1}$ at $25^{\circ}C$ and $107 Wh kg^{-1}$ at $-50^{\circ}C$ .

citations.quote: In summary, a commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon is fabricated in this work. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, the electrolyte additive adiponitrile (ADN) is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time, and the effects of the ADN on the performance improvement of the cathode material $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ are investigated for the first time. The results show that ADN can promote the formation of highly conductive and stable SEI film on the cathode material surface, and effectively improve the high-low-temperature performance and cycling stability of $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ as the cathode electrode material of sodium-ion batteries. In particular, the battery with 3% ADN shows the most obvious improvement, its discharge capacity increases by 10.5%, 8%, and 13% at the operating temperature of 45, -10, and -20 °C, respectively. For the cycling stability, the capacity retention rate of the battery without adding ADN drops rapidly to 75% after 40 cycles, while the capacity retention rate of the battery with 3% ADN can still reach 78% after 220 cycles. Adding ADN as electrolyte additive effectively improves the electrochemical performance of sodium ion batteries.

At a dewpoint of -40 °C, the electrolytes defined as G1, G2, G3, and G4 (Table 1) were injected into the cells. After packaging in vacuum at room temperature for 48 hours; the pouch cells were placed at the environment with 0.8 MPa and 45 °C and charged at 0.05 C for 180 min, followed by another charge at a constant current of 0.1 C for 360 min.

3.5. Enhanced electrochemical performance of HC anode
To elucidate the specific effects of NaTFPB additive on anode performance, a series of electrochemical performance tests were conducted using hard carbon (HC) as the anode material. Fig. 5a illustrates the rate capability of HC in different electrolyte systems. Specifically, at a current density of $30\mathrm{mA}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ , the system employing NaTFPB electrolyte exhibited an exceptional discharge specific capacity of $310\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ , significantly surpassing the $211\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ capacity of the Base electrolyte system. As the current density increased to $500\mathrm{mA}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ , the capacity of the Base electrolyte dropped dramatically to below $30\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ . In contrast, the NaTFPB electrolyte system demonstrated remarkable stability, maintaining a high discharge capacity of $174\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ , far exceeding the performance of the Base electrolyte. More notably, when the current density was reduced back to $30\mathrm{mA}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ , the capacity of the NaTFPB electrolyte system almost fully recovered to $306\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ . Furthermore, we conducted a comprehensive comparison of the cycling performance of HC anodes in different electrolytes at a current density of $30\mathrm{mA}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ (Fig. 5b). The results demonstrated that the NaTFPB electrolyte system exhibited exceptional cycling steadiness, maintaining a discharge specific capacity of $226.75\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ after 100 cycles, which significantly outperformed the capacity of the Base electrolyte (144.04 mAh $\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ ) under the same number of cycles. Additionally, it is noteworthy that the Base electrolyte suffered from excessive consumption of active $\mathrm{Na^{+}}$ during its formation process, resulting in an initial coulombic efficiency (CE) of only $60.40\%$ (Fig. 5c). The introduction of the NaTFPB additive effectively improves the utilization efficiency of active $\mathrm{Na^{+}}$ , thereby significantly enhancing the initial coulombic efficiency of the HC anode to $72.40\%$ (Fig. 5d).

2.1. Preparation of electrolytes
Sodium tetrakis[3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl]borate (NaTFPB, 99 % purity, sourced from Aladdin Biochemical Technology Co., Ltd.) were acquired as functional additives. Prior to their utilization, these additives underwent a rigorous freeze-drying process under vacuum conditions at $-80^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ for a duration of $24\mathrm{h}$ to remove $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ . The Base electrolyte was prepared by dissolving sodium hexafluorophosphate $(\mathrm{NaPF}_6, 1.0\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{L}^{-1})$ in a mixture of ethylene carbonate (EC) and dimethyl carbonate (DMC) (at a mass ratio of 1:1) containing $5.0\%$ fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC). The Base electrolyte serves as the reference for comparing the effect of the additive on the electrochemical performance of the cells. To formulate electrolytes containing functional additives, NaTFPB was added to the Base electrolyte at various concentrations, as illustrated in Fig. S1. All electrolyte preparations were carried out within an argon-filled glovebox environment, which was rigorously maintained to ensure that both water and oxygen levels were kept below $0.01~\mathrm{ppm}$ , thereby safeguarding the integrity and purity of the electrolytes.

## 配方筛选结果
获得文献支持的候选：cand-1-NaDFP。

### 候选资料：cand-1-NaDFP（通过筛选）
以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。
盐：NaPF6；浓度：0.8 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：0.8 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：EC, EMC；溶剂比例（基准待核对）：EC=0.3, EMC=0.7；添加剂：NaDFP；添加剂用量：NaDFP=1 wt% (optimal; saturation above 1 wt%)。
- 配方原文 [0002_Cai 等 - 2024 - A dual-functional electrolyte additive for stabilizing the solid electrolyte interphase and solvatio::sec4::child0]：EC, EMC, and sodium flurophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The electrolyte was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in a mixture of EC: EMC = 3:7, and this electrolyte was assigned as baseline electrolyte. NaDFP was added to the baseline electrolyte to prepare. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd and Hard Carbon were purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. Pouch cells were assembled using an NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1C), a hard carbon (HC, 290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05C) anode, and a Celgard 2700 membrane as the separator. NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. The HC active material, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), and conductive carbon black (Super P) with a mass ratio of 95:1.5:2:1.5 were mixed and dispersed in water, and then the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. The areal loading of the anode and cathode was 16 g m $^{-2}$ and 33 g m $^{-2}$ , respectively.

## 候选评估
### cand-1-NaDFP
评估建议：The candidate matches the paper's electrolyte (0.8 M NaPF6, EC:EMC 3:7, 1 wt% NaDFP) tested in hard-carbon||layered-oxide pouch full cells, and the paper directly reports an ICE increase after formation (84.69%→88.89%) plus improved -20 °C discharge capacity, supporting this intervention for the stated goal. No recorded computations were needed or available; the decision rests on literature evidence for this candidate.

- Electrolyte identity: 0.8 M NaPF6 in EC:EMC = 3:7 (the candidate's salt, concentration, and solvent ratio)：The paper prepares exactly 0.8 M NaPF6 dissolved in an EC:EMC = 3:7 mixture as the baseline electrolyte, matching the candidate's salt/concentration/solvent-ratio identity. [0002_Cai 等 - 2024 - A dual-functional electrolyte additive for stabilizing the solid electrolyte interphase and solvatio::sec4::child0]
- Additive NaDFP added at 1 wt%, stated to be the optimal concentration：The work adds NaDFP to the baseline and states 1 wt% is optimal because saturation occurs above 1 wt%, matching the candidate's additive and amount. [0002_Cai 等 - 2024 - A dual-functional electrolyte additive for stabilizing the solid electrolyte interphase and solvatio::sec7::child6]
- Hard-carbon || layered-oxide sodium-ion pouch full cell format：The electrolyte is tested in NFM (layered oxide) cathode / hard-carbon anode pouch cells assembled with 10 cathodes and 11 anodes, matching the required full-cell configuration. [0002_Cai 等 - 2024 - A dual-functional electrolyte additive for stabilizing the solid electrolyte interphase and solvatio::sec4::child0][0002_Cai 等 - 2024 - A dual-functional electrolyte additive for stabilizing the solid electrolyte interphase and solvatio::sec4::child1]
- -20 °C operation of the target full cell：Batteries with 1 wt% NaDFP were discharge-tested at -20 °C (and -30 °C), retaining 871/838/798 mAh vs 756/712/695 mAh for baseline, and the paper notes larger low-temperature gains than at room temperature. [0002_Cai 等 - 2024 - A dual-functional electrolyte additive for stabilizing the solid electrolyte interphase and solvatio::sec7::child8]
- Improvement of initial Coulombic efficiency after formation：Adding NaDFP raises the initial Coulombic efficiency from 84.69% to 88.89% and reduces gas production after formation, i.e., less capacity loss after formation. [0002_Cai 等 - 2024 - A dual-functional electrolyte additive for stabilizing the solid electrolyte interphase and solvatio::sec7::child3]
文献与候选的关联：The candidate composition (0.8 M NaPF6 in EC:EMC = 3:7 with 1 wt% NaDFP) is the exact electrolyte reported for NFM/HC pouch full cells. On these cells the paper reports the ICE gain after formation and the -20 °C discharge performance, so the ICE and low-temperature evidence are tied to the same candidate electrolyte and cell format; the half-cell CV discrepancy is explicitly noted and the paper argues the pouch-cell measurement is the relevant one. ### cand-2-CIE
评估建议：The candidate matches the study's designed CIE exactly (0.8 M NaPF6, G2:MO 7:3 vol), which is shown in the target HC||NFM pouch format at -20 °C and gives the highest HC ICE among the compared electrolytes; the only gap is that ICE at -20 °C in the pouch was not directly reported, so the recommendation is based on the exact composition match plus low-temperature pouch and half-cell ICE evidence.
